answer: Storage is bound to identity by a replication proof that is hard to satisfy with shared bytes, and because the sealed data is unique per identity, aliases and thin-provisioned clones fail the proof at their next challenge. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns a falcon, answers a cedar, and is named by an ember: a farm can mint ember bindings instantly, but the falcon behind each one is disk, and the cedar will catch the ones that share it. The attacker therefore pays for real storage per head.
